patients.label: Full-term female neonate with neonatal-onset familial HLH type 2 (PRF1)

identity_evidence.quote: We report a full-term female who developed abdominal distension

attribution_limitations: The NICU admission examination calls the infant hypotonic but a later sentence in the same examination states normal tone.

The authors list bicytopenia among the features supporting FHL2, while the next paragraph states that only 1 of 3 lineages met the HLH-2004 cytopenia threshold (hemoglobin and ANC did not). Table 1 interprets hemoglobin as mildly low, so bicytopenia (two low lineages) and the threshold count are compatible; both facts are kept.

The article states that hepatosplenomegaly documented at about 3 h of life most likely reflects limitations of immediate post-delivery palpation; the delivery-room examination is recorded as without hepatosplenomegaly.
The antenatal family-history statement does not say whose family it covers, and the amniocentesis results are described in a sentence about the mother.

The text states PT/aPTT/TT were prolonged, but the printed PT (23.6 s) and aPTT (96.3 s) lie inside the printed neonatal intervals (PT 12.7–26.6 s; aPTT 48.7–134.3 s); only TT (45.2 s) is outside its interval. PT and aPTT flags are left unknown.
